description: When a caller asks for JSON, does the agent emit JSON that actually validates — no prose wrapper, no invented fields, no stringified numbers?

cases.input: Extract the invoice number, total in dollars, and whether it is paid from this line, as JSON with keys invoiceNumber (string), total (number), paid (boolean) and nothing else: 'INV-2041 — $128.50 — settled 3 June'.
cases.rubric: The common structured-extraction shape: right keys, right JSON types, no extras. A stringified total is the usual failure.

cases.input: Classify the sentiment of 'the release slipped again' as JSON: {"sentiment": one of positive, neutral, negative}. Output only the JSON.
cases.rubric: Closed vocabulary: a near-miss label ('mixed', 'Negative.') is the failure mode a free-text check would wave through.

cases.input: List the three largest planets in the solar system as JSON: {"planets": [{"name": string, "rank": integer}]}. Output only the JSON.
cases.rubric: Nested array-of-objects is where schema adherence usually breaks: a bare array, or rank emitted as a string.

cases.input: Reply with only this JSON object and no other text: {"ok": true}
cases.rubric: 'Here is the JSON you asked for:' and ```json fences both break machine callers.
